denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Essential hypertension was first diagnosed on 2026-03-20, AFTER the policy start date 2023-11-22; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period – Claim ID 92d32bde-6f58-766d-27d5-0b9b1aa8eb33  

Claim Details:  
Patient Name – Jeraldine Santos Bins (Patient ID 92d32bde-6f58-766d-1ecc-bd45d93ec272)  
Date of Claim – 2026‑04‑19  
Policy – Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER) effective 2023‑11‑22  
Encounter – Virtual Follow‑up (VR) for Essential Hypertension, category Cardiac, total INR 300.00  

Grounds for Appeal – The diagnosis of Essential Hypertension was first recorded on 2026‑03‑20, which is after the policy start date of 2023‑11‑22. According to the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is NOT a Pre‑Existing Disease [suraksha_silver_policy#5].  

Consequently, the Pre‑Existing Disease waiting period of 36 months does not apply to this claim. Clause 4.2 explicitly limits the waiting period to conditions that meet the definition in Clause 2.2; since the condition does not meet that definition, the waiting period is inapplicable [suraksha_silver_policy#11].  

The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. No documentary evidence has been provided to demonstrate that the hypertension was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date, as required by the denial standards [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Clinical Necessity – Ongoing monitoring of hypertension after diagnosis or a medication change is medically necessary to prevent serious complications such as stroke, heart failure, and kidney disease. The clinical guideline recommends review every 4–6 weeks until control is achieved and then at regular intervals, including blood pressure measurement and screening for target‑organ damage [hypertension#3]. The treating physician will attach the relevant clinical notes confirming the need for the follow‑up encounter.  

Request – In view of the above, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 300.00 be paid in accordance with the policy terms.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Essential Hypertension — Diagnosis and Monitoring > Medical Necessity of Monitoring
citations.quote:
## Medical Necessity of Monitoring
After diagnosis or a medication change, review every 4–6 weeks until controlled, then every 3–6 months. Monitoring includes blood pressure measurement, electrolytes and creatinine, and screening for target-organ damage (ECG, urine albumin). Regular monitoring prevents stroke, heart failure and kidney disease.

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.
